source: Vinokurova N. Lexical Categories and Argument Structure: A Study with Reference to Sakha. Utrecht, 2005. (LOT Dissertation Series, no. 103)
topic: Unergative verbal roots and unergative verbs as √-suffix combinations
notes: Facts about passivization also support the lexically transitive status of second-type unergatives: they can undergo saturation both in the lexicon and in the syntax. As argued in 6.6, whether saturation is lexical or syntactic is revealed by the case marking on the remaining argument: nominative in the case of lexical and accusative in the case of syntactic passivization.
